thread:
anya: Heads-up — I'm starting a small integration of FlashAttention v3 into the serving runtime. Need quick alignment on kernel selection heuristics, KV cache interactions, and a safe rollout plan. TL;DR: local benches show some p95 regressions for long sequences under paged-attn.

sam: Quick perf notes from my microbench (A100-40G, batch_hint=16):
- model: small-llama-like, seq=512 -> flashv2 p50 9ms p95 28ms; flashv3 p50 8ms p95 30ms
- seq=1024 -> flashv2 p50 13ms p95 42ms; flashv3 p50 11ms p95 46ms
- seq=2048 -> flashv2 p50 25ms p95 88ms; flashv3 p50 22ms p95 120ms (noticeable p95 spike, seems tied to paged-attn path)

marco: That 120ms p95 at 2k is concerning. Do we know if this is pure kernel latency or extra memcpy/page faults when KV cache hot?

sam: Dived in with profiler. Observed extra host->device memcpy and increased page-fault-like stalls when KV cache > ~1k priming tokens. Also single-threaded memcpy on the CPU path when paged-attn tries to materialize blocked pages. Rough reproduction command: `./run_profile.sh --model=gpt-7b --seq=2048 --kv-priming=1024 --kernel=flashv3`

tess: Proposed runtime heuristics (draft):
```
features:
  flash_select: "cascade"
  flashv3_mode: "safemode"
  safemode_rules:
    - if seq > 1024 and kv_priming > 512 -> prefer flashv2
    - if host_page_faults > threshold -> prefer fused_attn or flashv2
    - if batch_size < 8 -> prefer flashv2
fallback_order: [fused_attn, flashv2]
```
Rationale: avoid paged-attn IO at high prefix sizes. Keep an opt-in flag for experiments.

anya: Good starting point. I want an explicit feature flag and an emergency circuit that forces fallback if we see regressions. Also need dashboards + specific guard thresholds.

marco: Suggested rollout + gating:
1) Local lab perf + perf-tests for many seq/kvs combos (automated)
2) Internal staging (0.5% internal traffic) for 12h
3) Canary 2% for non-enterprise traffic, hold 24h
4) Ramp: 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% (manual approvals at 10% and 30%)

At each stage gates: latency_p95(kernel=flashv3) <= latency_p95(kernel=flashv2) + 10ms absolute, error_rate increase <= 0.1% absolute, throughput >= 90% baseline. If any gate trips, flip to fallback for that pool and escalate.

sam: Adding monitoring queries to implement the gates:
- `inference_latency_p95{kernel=\"flashv3\", model=~\".*7b.*|.*13b.*\"}` vs `inference_latency_p95{kernel=\"flashv2\"}`
- `sum(rate(inference_errors_total{kernel=\"flashv3\"}[5m]))`
- Track `cuda_memcpy_count` and `host_page_faults` telemetry for the canary group.

ops-bot: Alert rule suggested: `alert if inference_latency_p95{kernel=\"flashv3\"} > inference_latency_p95{kernel=\"flashv2\"} + 10ms for 5m` -> runbook link + automatic flag flip.

tess: Also add a micro-profiling snapshot during canary windows capturing: memcpy bytes, kernel occupancy, page-fault-like stalls, and kv_cache_hit_ratio. Tag telemetry with `kernel_variant=flashv3_paged` to correlate.

anya: Ownership: I'll open the PR for the flag + heuristics and the smoke harness. Sam you attach perf artifacts & repro scripts. Marco you own the rollout gating config and alerts. Tess you own micro-profiling hooks and telemetry tags.

sam: Quick note: quantized/int8 paths show less p95 regression in tests — paging behavior differs. We'll run separate canaries for quantized workloads.

marco: Also consider kernel preference cascade: fused_attn -> flashv3 (non-paged) -> flashv3_paged -> flashv2. Some model families prefer fused kernels; prefer them when available.

tess: Practical checklist before canary: 
- [ ] feature flag `runtime.flashv3_safemode` with rollout API
- [ ] safemode heuristics implemented server-side (seq/kv/batch hints)
- [ ] unit + microbench tests added to CI
- [ ] dashboards & alerting rules created (p50/p95/err/throughput)
- [ ] deploy-bot circuit-breaker wiring for automatic fallback
- [ ] ops runbook & rollback snippet (one-click flag revert)
- [ ] 48h steady-state hold at 30% canary to observe tail behaviors

anya: I'll create the PR today and tag you all. Please comment tests and any missing metric.

sam: I'll upload the perf logs and a tiny flamegraph to the PR after I polish the repro. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Scheduled deployment: `flashv3-safemode-experiment` -> canary pool at 2201112400 UTC.

anya: Thanks — if nothing else, let's make sure the circuit is robust. I'll add a small note in the release notes about fallback behavior and the specific thresholds.

marco: One more operational tip: add a short-lived trace capture (5s) for any request that triggers fallback; include kernel selection reason in trace metadata. That will help root-cause KV vs kernel perf.

anya: Perfect. I'll include trace tagging in the PR.
